title: Administrator
description:
Legal Administrator - Temp to Perm

Location: York, YO1
Salary: 28,000 per annum
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9am-5pm
Contract: Temporary to Permanent

About the Role

We are recruiting for an Administrator to join a busy solicitors' firm based in York city centre.

This is a great opportunity for someone with previous administration or office support experience who is looking for a long-term position. You don't need to have worked in a legal environment, as full support will be provided, but you should be organised, proactive and confident handling a variety of administrative tasks.

Key Responsibilities
- Photocopying, scanning and preparing documents
- Preparing paperwork and correspondence
- Assisting with invoices and accounts administration
- Opening and maintaining files
- Obtaining documents and carrying out online searches
- Chasing clients and third parties by telephone and email
- Providing general administrative support to the wider team

What We're Looking For
- Previous administration or office support experience
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- Confidence using Microsoft Office and computer systems
- A professional telephone manner
- A positive attitude and the ability to work well within a team

Benefits
- 20 days' annual leave plus 8 bank holidays, increasing to 30 days with service
- 3 additional days off between Boxing Day and New Year
- Christmas Eve off when it falls on a normal working day
- An additional day off for your birthday after successful completion of probation
- Company pension and sick pay schemes, subject to eligibility
- Potential bonus scheme
- Subsidised parking
- Cycle-to-work scheme and corporate travel benefits
- Employee referral scheme offering up to 1,000 per referral
- Discounts on legal services and other in-house services, subject to qualifying periods

If you're an organised administrator looking for a varied role with the opportunity to secure a permanent position, we'd love to hear from you!

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

title: Assistant Buyer/Purchasing Assistant
description:
Assistant Buyer - Construction

Location: York
Salary: 28,000- 33,000 + package
Job Type: Permanent

We are currently recruiting for an Assistant Buyer to join an established construction business and support the procurement team across a range of construction projects.

This is an excellent opportunity for an Assistant Buyer, Junior Buyer, Procurement Assistant or construction professional with some purchasing experience who is looking to develop their career within a busy commercial and procurement environment.

The Role

Working closely with the Buyer and wider commercial team, you will assist with the procurement of materials, subcontract packages and services, ensuring projects are delivered on time and within budget.

Key Responsibilities
- Assist with the procurement of materials, plant, subcontractors and specialist services.
- Obtain and compare quotations from suppliers and subcontractors.
- Prepare and issue enquiries and purchase orders.
- Assist with negotiating competitive prices and commercial terms.
- Maintain accurate procurement records and supplier information.
- Monitor orders and ensure materials and services are delivered in line with project requirements.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers and subcontractors.
- Assist with reviewing supplier and subcontractor performance.
- Support the Buyer and Quantity Surveying team with procurement activities.
- Monitor market prices and identify potential cost savings.
- Assist with managing procurement schedules and ensuring deadlines are achieved.
- Liaise with site teams, Quantity Surveyors, Estimators and Project Managers.
- Ensure procurement is carried out in accordance with company procedures and project requirements.

About You

The successful candidate will ideally have:
- Previous experience within construction procurement, buying or purchasing.
- Knowledge of construction materials, subcontract packages and supply chains.
- Strong communication and negotiation skills.
- Good commercial awareness and attention to detail.
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel.
- The ability to manage multiple enquiries and deadlines.
- A proactive approach and willingness to develop within the role.

Candidates with experience as a Trainee Buyer, Junior Buyer, Procurement Assistant, Assistant Quantity Surveyor, Estimator or Commercial Assistant who are looking to move into construction procurement will also be considered.

Career Development

This role offers the opportunity to develop your procurement and commercial knowledge while working alongside experienced construction professionals, with clear potential to progress towards Buyer and Senior Buyer positions.

Apply today for more information and a confidential discussion about this opportunity.

title: HR Administrator
description:
Sewell Wallis is looking for an HR Administrator to join a professional services business, based on-site just near Wetherby.

You ll have 4-5 years' experience in HR/recruitment and have a good understanding of employment law and HR requirements. It is not necessary that you have a CIPD qualification, but that would benefit an application. This role would suit someone who is keen to progress, learn and get stuck into the business; you ll have a positive can-do attitude and work closely with the HR director day-to-day.

Responsibilities include supporting employee relations and case management, maintaining accurate HR records and systems, processing contracts and leavers, and ensuring compliance with employment legislation and data protection requirements.

What will you be doing?
- Employee Relations: Provide administrative support for employee relations matters, including disciplinary, grievance and performance cases, arranging meetings, preparing documentation, taking accurate notes and maintaining confidential records.
- Recruitment: Support the end-to-end recruitment process, including preparing job adverts, screening applications, coordinating interviews, communicating with candidates and supporting hiring managers.
- Onboarding & Offboarding: Coordinate new starter processes, including contracts, right-to-work checks, DBS checks where required, inductions and probation reviews, as well as supporting leavers and internal employee changes.
- HR Administration: Maintain accurate employee records and HR systems, including holiday, sickness, absence, contract and employee information, ensuring records are updated accurately and within required deadlines.
- Employee Support: Act as a first point of contact for routine HR queries, providing support to employees and managers regarding HR processes, policies, pay, benefits and employment documentation.
- Training & Compliance: Coordinate training and e-learning activities, support performance and absence management, maintain HR policies and job descriptions, and assist with health and safety and compliance activities.
- Payroll & Benefits: Support payroll, benefits, salary reviews and employee changes by providing accurate information, preparing documentation and liaising with relevant internal teams.
- Reporting & Data Protection: Prepare HR reports and metrics, maintain effective filing and document retention systems, and ensure HR processes and records comply with data protection, confidentiality and internal policies.

What skills are we looking for?
- Confident written and verbal communication skills, with a friendly, professional and approachable manner.
- Experience working within an HR or business administration setting.
- Strong organisational and administrative abilities, with excellent attention to detail.
- A basic understanding of UK employment law and HR policies.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Outlook, Word and Excel.
- The ability to manage sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
- Experience assisting with or coordinating meetings, especially those relating to employee relations.
- Currently studying towards, holding, or interested in pursuing a CIPD Level 3 qualification.
- Based locally to the office and able to travel independently using your own transport.

What's on offer?
- £28,000 - £30,000 starting salary
- 20 days annual leave plus 8 statutory bank holidays, with the addition of Christmas shutdown and your birthday off!
- Company pension scheme
- Company sick pay
- Parking available

Send us your CV below, or contact Inci Evcil for more information.

To apply, please send your CV, quoting our reference and specifying which website you saw this position advertised on. Due to the high volume of applications, please accept that if we have not responded to your application within seven days, your application has not been successful. Sewell Wallis is a specialist recruitment company with a vast amount of experience in our industry. We offer permanent, temporary and interim recruitment support for accounting and finance, human resources and business support positions. We recruit at all levels within finance, from Purchase Ledger Administrator and Credit Controller level through to Financial Controller and Director positions. We are well situated to cover all of South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire and Manchester. Please visit our website for more information on accountancy and finance jobs and human resources or business support positions.

title: Paralegal
company: LSL Property Services plc - Agency - Permanent
description:
LSL is a one of the largest providers of services to mortgage intermediaries, specialist mortgage and protection advice to estate agency and new build customers and valuation services to the UK's biggest mortgage lenders. It also operates a network of owned and franchised estate agency branches.

Based within our Group Legal Team in York, we are looking to recruit a Paralegal to provide support to the Group Legal Team with a wide variety of matters spanning across all areas of the LSL Group.

Location: York - on site office-based.

Role Purpose

To provide legal and administrative support to the Legal Team, assisting with a broad range of legal matters and ensuring the efficient delivery of legal services across the business. The role supports solicitors, contract administration, regulatory compliance, and corporate transactions whilst maintaining high standards of accuracy and professionalism.

Key Responsibilities
- Conduct legal research and prepare summaries, reports, and recommendations.
- Draft, review, and amend legal documents, including contracts, NDAs, agreements, and correspondence.
- Support solicitors and legal professionals on commercial, corporate, regulatory, and dispute resolution matters.
- Assist with contract management, document control, and legal record keeping.
- Monitor legal deadlines and maintain case and matter tracking systems.
- Prepare documentation for corporate transactions and business projects.
- Support regulatory and compliance activities.
- Liaise with internal stakeholders and external legal advisers where required.
- Assist with updating policies, procedures, and customer-facing terms and conditions.
- Ensure confidential information is handled appropriately at all times.

Knowledge, Skills & Experience
- Law degree, Legal Practice qualification, or equivalent legal education.
- Previous paralegal experience desirable but not essential.
- Strong legal research and analytical skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong organisational and time-management abilities.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and legal document management systems.
- Commercial awareness and understanding of legal risk.

Key Competencies
- Analytical thinking
- Attention to detail
- Professional integrity
- Communication and influencing
- Organisation and planning
- Problem solving
- Teamwork and collaboration
- Customer and stakeholder focus

Apply

Dealing with samples. Providing clerical assistance to Practice and Trust staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning. Ordering, re-ordering and monitoring of stationery and other supplies. Dealing with clinical waste. Provision of refreshments for staff and visitors as required; loading and emptying the dishwasher and keeping the kitchen area clean and tidy.
